To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

region-specific responses of phenylpropane metabolism and control of iron homeostasis are important for the maintenance and inhibition of elongation in the apical and basal portions of soybean primary roots in response to water deficit.
region-specific regulation in the soybean root tip is related to phenylpropanoids, which may contribute to growth maintenance and inhibition, respectively, in region 1 and region 2.
In water-stressed primary roots, growth is inhibited in the elongation region, but maintained at well-water rates in the apically most elongating 4 mm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of growth responses to water stress in two distinct regions of the elongation zone of the soybean primary roots.
the regulation of the response of the elongation zone to water stress in soybean.
the regulation of growth response to soil water deficits in the soybean root.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

region-specific growth responses to water stress in soybean roots involve a coordinated regulation of the biosynthesis of phenylproanoids, including isoflavonoids, and the accumulation of lignin in the elongation zones.
the maintenance of growth in region 1 of water-stressed soybeans is due to the accumulation of isoflavones, while the inhibition of growth is due to accumulation of lignins in region 2.

the growth response to water deficit in the soybean root tip involves the regulation of multiple metabolic processes, including phenylpropanoids and protection from oxidative damage, in a spatially and temporally regulated manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

water stress in the elongation zones of the primary roots of both soybean and maize causes the up-regulation of several stress-related proteins, including those that may be involved in the regulation of growth responses.

the distinct growth response of the elongation zone in soybean roots under water stress may result from region-specific regulation of isoflavone and lignin metabolism, and control of free intracellular iron.
the growth response to water deficit is region-specific in both maize and soybean primary roots.
The main takeaway from our work is that
region 2 of soybean roots is a highly dynamic region, with many changes in protein abundance that may contribute to the growth inhibition under water stress.
the regulation of phenyl-propanoid metabolism and free-iron levels in the elongation region are critical to the regulation of growth in response to water deficit.
the soybean primary roots respond differently to water deficit in the apical and elongating zones.
